newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South African long bonds shook off some of their midday weakness in late afternoon trade on Tuesday after a swathe of rumours swept the market, taking yields as high as 15.20 percent.
Dealers said short-covering helped the key R150 long bond return to the 15.14 percent level by 1400 GMT, some nine basis points above its level at the same time on Monday.
"People got a little bit carried away earlier and had to cover their positions. The U.S. T-bond has also come back a little," one bond trader said.
The 30-year Treasury was last trading at 6.95 percent retracing from 6.98 percent late on Monday.

South African bonds, after beginning the day on a steady footing, began weakening later in the morning on selling emanating from two London banks and as jobbers jumped on the band-wagon, dealers said.

Rumours that the central Reserve Bank was selling stock in the market as part of its funding activities helped to push yields up. "The Bank could be funding. It would not be unusual as they are preparing for their financial year end," one dealer said.
Traders said there was talk that the Bank was selling longer-dated R153 bonds in a bid to cover some of its losses on its forward cover book.

Another negative was speculation from London that local municipalities were about to default on loan repayments. This may have been sparked by comments from Provincial Affairs Minister Valli Moosa earlier on the "unviability" of some councils.
The finance department said later it was not aware of any major debt default by municipalities.

"I have no knowledge of that whatsoever, of local authorities failing or anything of the sort. It is news to me and I would imagine it is just a rumour," Coen Kruger, chief director of asset and liability management, told Reuters.
Other dealers said market weakness was due to a breakthrough on the upside of a key technical level at 15.04 percent.
"I spoke to a lot of people this morning and they all said if 15.04 breaks they were getting out," a trader said.
Dealers said bonds were seen testing upper levels again on Wednesday although good demand would emerge at the 15.14 percent and 15.19 levels.
The rand ended two cents stronger after a choppy, but quiet, day tracking the bond market, dealers said.

Overnight demand from United States on Monday and follow through from London early in the morning initially propelled the unit firmer, only for it to retrace most of its gains as bonds weakened towards noon.
But a slight recovery in bonds in the afternoon again pushed the local currency firmer.
Dealers said the rand would be eyeing action from New York on Tuesday night amid concerns that the unit was bought too strongly.
"It might have been a bit overdone last night, some of it bond-related. But today there was some foreign (bond) selling which may take it a little weaker."
The rand ended at 4.4145/4175 on the dollar from a 4.4345/4375 close on Monday.
Against the crosses, the rand was last quoted at 7.0014/0106 against sterling from 7.0499/0591 on Monday and at 0.3809/3812 marks from 0.3803/3806 previously.
On the money market, three-month deposit rates held steady at 16.50 to 16.55 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate maintained its recent 15.90 to 16.10 percent range.
The Reserve Bank said the money market shortage edged up to 9.896 billion rand on Monday from 9.602 billion rand on Saturday.
The Bond Exchange said that foreigners bought a net 839.48 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Monday after buying 30.29 million rand's worth on Friday.
Nominal cumulative volumes on the bond market amounted to 5.52 billion rand on Monday compared with 9.36 billion on Friday.
-- Nicole Mordant, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
